title: The lint checks for self in fn parameters that specify the Self-type explicitly
summary: Increases the amount and decreases the readability of code Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: It detects useless calls to str::as_bytes() before calling len() or is_empty().
summary: The len() and is_empty() methods are also directly available on strings, and they return identical results. In particular, len() on a string returns the number of bytes. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of bitwise and/or operators between booleans, where performance may be improved by using a lazy and.
summary: The bitwise operators do not support short-circuiting, so it may hinder code performance. Additionally, boolean logic “masked” as bitwise logic is not caught by lints like unnecessary_fold Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for expressions of the form if c { true } else { false } (or vice versa) and suggests using the condition directly.
summary: Redundant code. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for expressions of the form if c { x = true } else { x = false } (or vice versa) and suggest assigning the variable directly from the condition.
summary: Redundant code. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for address of operations (&) that are going to be dereferenced immediately by the compiler.
summary: Suggests that the receiver of the expression borrows the expression. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for bindings that needlessly destructure a reference and borrow the inner value with &ref.
summary: This pattern has no effect in almost all cases. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for borrow operations (&) that are used as a generic argument to a function when the borrowed value could be used.
summary: Suggests that the receiver of the expression borrows the expression. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks if an iterator is used to check if a string is ascii.
summary: The str type already implements the is_ascii method. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for functions collecting an iterator when collect is not needed.
summary: collect causes the allocation of a new data structure, when this allocation may not be needed. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: The lint checks for if-statements appearing in loops that contain a continue statement in either their main blocks or their else-blocks, when omitting the else-block possibly with some rearrangement of code can make the code easier to understand.
summary: The lint also checks if the last statement in the loop is a continue Having explicit else blocks for if statements containing continue in their THEN branch adds unnecessary branching and nesting to the code. Having an else block containing just continue can also be better written by grouping the statements following the whole if statement within the THEN block and omitting the else block completely. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for fn main() { .. } in doctests
summary: The test can be shorter (and likely more readable) if the fn main() is left implicit. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for empty else branches.
summary: An empty else branch does nothing and can be removed. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of for_each that would be more simply written as a for loop.
summary: for_each may be used after applying iterator transformers like filter for better readability and performance. It may also be used to fit a simple operation on one line. But when none of these apply, a simple for loop is more idiomatic. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for empty if branches with no else branch.
summary: It can be entirely omitted, and often the condition too. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for late initializations that can be replaced by a let statement with an initializer.
summary: Assigning in the let statement is less repetitive. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for lifetime annotations which can be removed by relying on lifetime elision.
summary: The additional lifetimes make the code look more complicated, while there is nothing out of the ordinary going on. Removing them leads to more readable code. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for unnecessary match or match-like if let returns for Option and Result when function signatures are the same.
summary: This match block does nothing and might not be what the coder intended. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Lints ?Sized bounds applied to type parameters that cannot be unsized
summary: The ?Sized bound is misleading because it cannot be satisfied by an unsized type Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for no-op uses of Option::{as_deref, as_deref_mut}, for example, Option<&T>::as_deref() returns the same type.
summary: Redundant code and improving readability. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for calling take function after as_ref.
summary: Redundant code. take writes None to its argument. In this case the modification is useless as it’s a temporary that cannot be read from afterwards. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: The lint checks for parenthesis on literals in range statements that are superfluous.
summary: Having superfluous parenthesis makes the code less readable overhead when reading. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Check if a &mut function argument is actually used mutably.
summary: Less mut means less fights with the borrow checker. It can also lead to more opportunities for parallelization. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for functions taking arguments by value, but not consuming them in its body.
summary: Taking arguments by reference is more flexible and can sometimes avoid unnecessary allocations. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of pub(self) and pub(in self).
summary: It’s unnecessary, omitting the pub entirely will give the same results. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Suggests replacing Ok(x?) or Some(x?) with x in return positions where the ? operator is not needed to convert the type of x.
summary: There’s no reason to use ? to short-circuit when execution of the body will end there anyway. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for looping over the range of 0..len of some collection just to get the values by index.
summary: Just iterating the collection itself makes the intent more clear and is probably faster because it eliminates the bounds check that is done when indexing. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for raw string literals with an unnecessary amount of hashes around them.
summary: It’s just unnecessary, and makes it look like there’s more escaping needed than is actually necessary. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for raw string literals where a string literal can be used instead.
summary: For consistent style by using simpler string literals whenever possible. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for return statements at the end of a block.
summary: Removing the return and semicolon will make the code more rusty. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for return statements on Err paired with the ? operator.
summary: The return is unnecessary. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of str::splitn (or str::rsplitn) where using str::split would be the same.
summary: The function split is simpler and there is no performance difference in these cases, considering that both functions return a lazy iterator. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for bindings (constants, statics, or let bindings) that are defined with one numeric type but are consistently cast to a different type in all usages.
summary: If a binding is always cast to a different type when used, it would be clearer and more efficient to define it with the target type from the start. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for needlessly including a base struct on update when all fields are changed anyway.
summary: This will cost resources (because the base has to be somewhere), and make the code less readable. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for the usage of negated comparison operators on types which only implement PartialOrd (e.g., f64).
summary: These operators make it easy to forget that the underlying types actually allow not only three potential Orderings (Less, Equal, Greater) but also a fourth one (Uncomparable). This is especially easy to miss if the operator based comparison result is negated. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for multiplication by -1 as a form of negation.
summary: It’s more readable to just negate. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for negative feature names with prefix no- or not-
summary: Features are supposed to be additive, and negatively-named features violate it. Clippy puts this lint in the cargo group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for loops that will always break, return or continue an outer loop.
summary: This loop never loops, all it does is obfuscating the code. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks for new not returning a type that contains Self.
summary: As a convention, new methods are used to make a new instance of a type. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for public types with a pub fn new() -> Self method and no implementation of Default.
summary: The user might expect to be able to use Default as the type can be constructed without arguments. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.
